This article compares the distribution of the [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score for incident atrial fibrillation patients across [[danmark|Danmark]] and its five administrative regions. The CHA2DS2-VASc score is a clinical tool used to estimate stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation. Based on the available data from 2023, a total of 19,671 incident patients were recorded nationally, with an overall average score of 1.73 and a median of 2.00 [^src1]. 

Because the dataset contains only a single dated section, no longitudinal trends can be established regarding whether regional stroke risk profiles are improving or declining over time. Furthermore, the source data does not define specific clinical targets or thresholds for these regional averages, meaning no met or missed targets can be evaluated.

When comparing the regions, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] recorded the highest average CHA2DS2-VASc score at 1.82, indicating a slightly higher baseline stroke risk profile among its 3,202 incident patients [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] had the lowest average score at 1.66, despite having the largest patient volume with 5,241 recorded cases [^src1]. The remaining regions fell between these two extremes: [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] both averaged 1.75, while [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] averaged 1.71 [^src1]. 

The spread of scores is highly consistent across the country. Every region, as well as the national aggregate, shares the same median (2.00), minimum (0.00), and maximum (6.00) values [^src1]. The standard deviation also shows minimal variation, ranging narrowly from 1.06 in Region Syddanmark and Region Midtjylland to 1.08 in Region Hovedstaden [^src1]. There were no unreported (uoplyst) scores in any region, ensuring complete data coverage across all 19,671 patients [^src1]. While Region Sjælland and Region Hovedstaden sit at the opposite ends of the average spectrum, the narrow absolute difference of 0.16 points suggests that the baseline stroke risk distribution among incident patients is relatively uniform across Denmark.
